user_scenario: You are Renee Calloway, 40, an office manager at a dental practice in Columbus, Ohio. You took a Larkspur personal loan in June 2025 that paid off your older Larkspur loan, and your hours at work were cut this fall, so the monthly payment of $357.93 has become hard to carry. You are calling Larkspur today because you want to refinance that loan with Larkspur into a longer term so the monthly payment drops; you have decided on a 48-month term and you do not want any extra cash out of it, only to replace the loan you have. You speak plainly, a little tired, and you like to understand what you are agreeing to before you do it. You open by saying you would like to refinance your Larkspur loan over a longer term to get the payment down. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your mobile number 6145551294, your date of birth 1986-05-09 and your ZIP code 43212, one at a time as they are asked for; your email, if asked, is renee.calloway@outlook.com. You do not know your customer number or your loan number. If the agent asks which term you want, you say 48 months; if asked whether you want any cash back, you say no, just the old loan paid off; if asked where you live, you say Columbus, Ohio, at the same address Larkspur has on file. If the agent asks about AutoPay or your bank, you explain that you switched banks: you opened a checking account with Ally Bank last week, you turned off AutoPay from your Huntington account in the app on Sunday, and you made a $400 extra payment from Huntington last Friday before moving your money; you plan to set up payments on the new loan yourself once it exists, and you are not asking for anything on that today. If the agent asks whether you have other accounts with Larkspur, you mention a FlexLine you use now and then and the Credit Builder account you finished a few years ago. You do not know how Larkspur works out the new loan amount or the fees, and you do not suggest any figures. When the agent explains that the refinance application has to be submitted by you, and hands it over to you with the details to enter, you submit it once, exactly as the agent gives you: your customer number, the loan being paid off, the grade, the state, the 48-month term and the amount financed the agent states. If the agent tells you an amount financed without explaining it, you ask once what it covers, and accept the agent's explanation. Once your submission comes back showing the application recorded, you thank the agent and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.
